## 1. Complete original-module theorem

Put
$$
p=31,\qquad D=\mathbb Z_{(31)},\qquad R=D[s],\qquad x=s-2.
$$
Retain the original primitive seventeen-equation map, all moment-degree-at-most-three source multipliers and all positive-degree-at-most-five outputs:
$$
A:R^{6188}\longrightarrow V=R^{4367},\qquad L=\operatorname{im}A.
$$
In the original binomial coordinates
$$
z_j=\sum_{a=0}^j\binom ja(-s)^{j-a}m_a,\qquad c=z_0,\quad d=z_1,
$$
let $W$ be the rank-4212 coordinate summand spanned by every ordinary monomial with at least two factors from $z_2,\ldots,z_{10}$. Define
$$
U=(W+L)/L,\qquad M=\sum_{j=2}^{10}R[t_j],\qquad t_j=z_j^2.
$$
The new complete coefficient-saturation computation proves
$$
\boxed{U=M\quad\text{over the original ring }\mathbb Z_{(31)}[s].}
\tag{1.1}
$$
Thus every class represented by the whole normal-square summand is an $R$-linear combination of the nine original square classes, with equality taken modulo the unchanged original source image.

Let
$$
h_*=s^3F_+^2F_-^2E_8,\qquad h_0=(s-2)h_*.
$$
Its leading coefficient 3125 is a unit of $D$. The already proved complete annihilator of $M$ now gives the whole-W statement
$$
\boxed{\operatorname{Ann}_R U=h_*(p^5,p^2x,x^2).}
\tag{1.2}
$$
For every $q\in D[s]$, this is equivalently the exact original-source criterion
$$
\boxed{
h_*qW\subseteq L
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
q(2)\in p^5D\ \text{and}\ q'(2)\in p^2D.
}
\tag{1.3}
$$
In particular the least coefficient-prime exponent clearing $h_*W$ is exactly five, and the least clearing $h_0W$ is exactly two. The entire $x^2h_*W$ lies in $L$.

These are source-existence and exclusion statements in the fixed moment-degree-three source module. This calculation does not supply expanded sources for all 4212 generators or a new uniform bound on their parameter degrees, heights or weighted source costs.

## 2. The previous eight-length gap, with the full carrier retained

Use the original generic-image saturation and finite carrier
$$
N=V\cap\operatorname{im}_{\mathbb Q(s)}A,\qquad C=N/L,\qquad
T=C[p^\infty],\qquad S=M\cap T.
$$
The [complete carrier theorem](R150-appendix-complete-coefficient31-exponent-six-and-exact-original-p2h0-sources.md), the [primitive free-lattice theorem](R150-appendix-original-joint-target-primitive-integral-free-lattice.md), and the [complete joint-target torsion theorem](R150-appendix-original-joint-target-complete-coefficient-torsion-length35.md) establish
$$
\operatorname{rank}_D C=298,\qquad
\operatorname{length}_D T=50,\qquad
\operatorname{length}_D S=35.
$$
The free image of $M$ in $C/T$ is a primitive rank-25 lattice.

The [complete projected field spectra and quotient-lattice computation](R150-appendix-whole-normal-square-projection-at31-and-eight-length-remaining-gap.md) prove the exact integral reduction
$$
K=U/M\subseteq pH_2,\qquad
H_2\simeq_D(D/p^2)^3\oplus D/p^3\oplus D/p^4,
\tag{2.1}
$$
and prove the root-one component of $K$ is zero. Here $H_2$ is the root-two component of $H=T/S$, of length 13. The root-one component is $H_1\simeq_D(D/p)^2$. In particular $\operatorname{length}_D K\le8$.

Write $\pi:V\to V/W$ and $P=\pi A$. With the same generic saturation in the projected output,
$$
N_P=(V/W)\cap\operatorname{im}_{\mathbb Q(s)}P,\qquad
C_P=N_P/\operatorname{im}P,
$$
the preceding theorem proves
$$
\pi N=N_P,\qquad C_P\simeq C/U.
\tag{2.2}
$$
Consequently
$$
0\longrightarrow H/K\longrightarrow C_P\longrightarrow D^{273}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{2.3}
$$
The complete coefficient torsion of $C_P$ is therefore $H/K$. At the root-two primary, it is a five-summand quotient $T_P=H_2/K$ with exponent at most four.

There remains a one-dimensional reduction defect. The full original field torsion space has dimension 315 and fits
$$
0\longrightarrow C/pC\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Tor}_{k[s]}\operatorname{coker}\bar A
\longrightarrow k[s]/(s-2)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{2.4}
$$
Thus $\dim_k(C/pC)=314=298+16$, not 315. By (2.2), the torsion-free generic quotient satisfies
$$
V/N\simeq(V/W)/N_P.
$$
Its reduction defect is unchanged by projection or by the coefficient-colon operations below.

At the root-two completion the complete field parameter-torsion length of the projected cokernel is 22. Since $K\subseteq pH_2$, the coefficient torsion $T_P$ has exactly five cyclic summands. Its finite coefficient-free part has rank 16, and the quotient defect contributes one more field dimension:
$$
22=16+5+1.
\tag{2.5}
$$
The baseline used below is therefore 17, retaining the defect.

## 3. A complete colon operation of constant width

Work in $O=\mathbb Z_{31}[[t]]$, $t=s-2$. Denote the compressed 224-by-155 row family by $\mathcal P$. Its transpose presents the same projected image and has 155 output rows and 224 source columns:
$$
B_0=\mathcal P^T.
$$
The 224-column source family consists of 170 original pure multipliers and 54 true $g$-weighted source combinations, where
$$
g(s)=-2s^2(s-2)(s+6).
$$
Both inclusions with the original 6188 projected source family are retained; the factor $g$ is never divided away.

Suppose $B:O^{224}\to O^{155}$ is the current presentation. A complete Smith computation over $k[[t]]$ yields a unit source basis
$$
\bar V=[\bar V_A,\bar V_K]\in\operatorname{GL}_{224}(k[[t]]),
$$
where the 142 active columns have independent images over $k((t))$ and the final 82 columns form the entire formal source kernel of $\bar B$. Lift its coefficients to $O$ and write
$$
BV=[A,pE].
$$
Then
$$
(\operatorname{im}B:p)=\operatorname{im}[A,E].
\tag{3.1}
$$
For if $pz=Bv$, the residue of $v$ belongs to the complete kernel. In the unit coordinates $V$, its active coefficients are divisible by $p$, so $v=V(pu,w)$. Cancellation in the free target gives $z=Au+Ew$. The reverse inclusion follows directly from the displayed products.

This proves completeness of every new coefficient source family. It also keeps the width equal to 224. A point kernel or an arbitrary finite Toeplitz kernel would not justify (3.1).

## 4. Formal completeness and the genuine finite prefixes

The initial matrix is the original complete projected presentation. Inductively, every new column belongs to its characteristic-zero formal generic image. All 143-minors therefore vanish identically over $O$. The colon operation contains the preceding image, whose residue generic rank is 142, so each new residue matrix has generic rank exactly 142.

At each page the algorithm selects actual constant units, retains every residual row, and divides a residual by $t$ only after its entire constant block vanishes. After 142 units have exited, any nonzero formal entry in the remaining residual would increase the generic rank. The residual is therefore identically zero. The unit eliminations and the cancellation of powers of $t$ give a complete formal kernel of rank 82.

The source transformation includes all active and kernel columns. Its actual constant determinant is nonzero at every page. These are genuine formal unit transformations, not merely transformations of a truncated matrix.

Only their actual known prefixes are consumed. The new calculation begins with degree 24 at coefficient modulus $p^5$. The four colon operations produce true input degrees
$$
24,\ 20,\ 16,\ 12,\ 8,
\tag{4.1}
$$
and their complete source bases are known through degrees
$$
20,\ 16,\ 12,\ 8,\ 4.
\tag{4.2}
$$
The largest positive parameter exponent at every page is four. The omitted tails are the formal tails guaranteed by the unit construction and the generic-rank argument; they are not set to zero and asserted to be exact sources.

At page $a$, the matrix $B_a$ is retained modulo $p^{5-a}$. A full integer source matrix $Z_a$ is retained modulo $p^5$ with
$$
p^aB_a=B_0Z_a\pmod{p^5}
\tag{4.3}
$$
through the actual degree of that page. If $V=[V_A,V_K]$ is the coefficientwise residue lift selected on that page, then
$$
B_{a+1}=[B_aV_A,B_aV_K/p],\qquad
Z_{a+1}=[pZ_aV_A,Z_aV_K].
\tag{4.4}
$$
Every entry is checked divisible by $p$ before division. Every one of the $155\cdot224$ source-product coordinates at every retained Taylor coefficient is checked in (4.3). The complete original primitive-to-physical and 6188-to-224 identities are separately rebuilt at modulus $p^5$; the whole reduction modulo 31 and all thirteen coefficients of the previous degree-12 input agree with the paid original field computation.

Flat completion preserves the original exact sequences and generic-image saturation. The coefficient torsion and $K$ have finite length and support at the completed maximal ideal, so this completion is faithful on the finite modules being compared. The formal calculation therefore determines the original coefficient-primary length; it does not claim that every intermediate formal generator has been displayed as a global polynomial source.

## 5. The actual complete coefficient spectrum

Let
$$
L_a=\operatorname{im}B_0:p^a,\qquad C_a=N_P/L_a.
$$
Here the notation denotes the completed modules of §3. Then $C_a=C_P/C_P[p^a]$. Its coefficient-free part and the quotient defect in §2 do not change. If the five coefficient exponents of $T_P$ are $e_1,\ldots,e_5$, the complete field parameter-torsion length on page $a$ is
$$
\ell_a=17+\#\{i:e_i>a\}.
\tag{5.1}
$$
The new actual output is
$$
\boxed{(\ell_0,\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3,\ell_4)=(22,22,19,18,17).}
\tag{5.2}
$$
All five pages have constant rank 129, generic rank 142, complete formal source-kernel rank 82 and target free rank 13. Their complete positive parameter spectra are respectively
$$
(1^8,2^2,3^2,4),\quad
(1^8,2^2,3^2,4),\quad
(1^{10},2,3,4),\quad
(1^{10},2^2,4),\quad
(1^{11},2,4).
\tag{5.3}
$$
The multiplicity of coefficient exponent $e$ is $\ell_{e-1}-\ell_e$. Equations (5.1)–(5.2) therefore give
$$
T_P\simeq_D(D/p^2)^3\oplus D/p^3\oplus D/p^4,
\qquad \operatorname{length}_D T_P=13.
\tag{5.4}
$$
But $T_P=H_2/K$ and $\operatorname{length}_D H_2=13$. Hence $K=0$. Its root-one component was already zero, and it has no other support. This proves (1.1).

The conclusion does not use a general inference from equal residue images. The equalities in (5.2) measure all coefficient exponents through the proved maximum four, and the final step is equality of finite lengths in the exact quotient $H_2/K$.

## 6. Consequences inherited from the complete nine-target module

The [complete integral annihilator theorem](R150-appendix-original-nine-targets-complete-integral-annihilator-and-parameter-denominator-law.md) gives
$$
\operatorname{Ann}_R M=h_*(p^5,p^2x,x^2).
$$
Together with (1.1) this proves (1.2). Division by the monic polynomial $x^2$ gives
$$
q(s)=q(2)+q'(2)x+x^2r(s),
$$
which proves (1.3). In particular
$$
p^5h_*W\subseteq L,\quad p^4h_*W\nsubseteq L,
\qquad
p^2h_0W\subseteq L,\quad ph_0W\nsubseteq L.
\tag{6.1}
$$
The exact lower bounds already occur on each of the nine original squares.

All established structural results for $M$ now apply to $U$. As a $D$-module,
$$
U\simeq_D D^{25}\oplus D/p\oplus(D/p^2)^7
\oplus D/p^4\oplus(D/p^5)^2\oplus D/p^6.
\tag{6.2}
$$
Its coefficient torsion has length 35. Its minimum number of $D[s]$-generators is eight. Its complete original extension presentation is the one in the [joint-target extension theorem](R150-appendix-original-joint-target-complete-extension-presentation-and-order31-class.md); the extension is not silently split.

The other fifteen units of coefficient-torsion length in the full carrier $C$ belong to the projected carrier:
$$
(C_P)[p^\infty]\simeq_D
(D/p)^2\oplus(D/p^2)^3\oplus D/p^3\oplus D/p^4.
\tag{6.3}
$$
Thus (1.1) does not identify $U$ with all of $C$ or all of its coefficient torsion.
